description: Figure 2 presents a bar chart illustrating the average accuracy across eleven datasets for various training methods. The horizontal axis displays the training methods, labeled as “Standard,” “CINQS,” and “CINQS-VLM,” listed in that order. The vertical axis represents average accuracy, labeled as “Avg. accuracy across 11 datasets,” with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, and tick marks at 10-unit intervals. Three bars are present for each training method, representing performance on the “LLaVA-W,” “Imagen,” and “LLaVA-Wild” datasets, visually distinguished by shades of blue. For the “Standard” method, the “LLaVA-W” bar is approximately 60.2, the “Imagen” bar is around 52.6, and the “LLaVA-Wild” bar is approximately 55.9. For “CINQS,” the “LLaVA-W” bar is approximately 82.6, the “Imagen” bar is around 88.8, and the “LLaVA-Wild” bar is approximately 79.5. Finally, for “CINQS-VLM,” the “LLaVA-W” bar is approximately 82.1, the “Imagen” bar is around 90.1, and the “LLaVA-Wild” bar is approximately 82.6. The bars are grouped by training method, with each group containing three bars representing the three datasets. No bars are visually emphasized, and the chart does not indicate any specific sorting order.
